claims.claim: A polysaccharide from an ancient Chinese herb alters gut microbial communities and influences neural pathways linked to aging.
claims.episode_span: Researchers examined a polysaccharide extracted from an ancient Chinese herb and its effects on aging markers. The compound altered gut microbial communities in ways that influenced neural pathways linked to aging processes.
claims.source_title: Ancient Chinese Herb Polysaccharide Slows Aging Through Gut and Brain Pathways
claims.supporting_quote: Ancient Chinese Herb Polysaccharide Slows Aging Through Gut and Brain Pathways

claims.claim: At least an 89 percent probability exists that Paris Agreement low-emission targets would reduce Antarctic ice loss by 2100 compared with high-emission scenarios.
claims.episode_span: The analysis gave at least an 89 percent probability that Paris Agreement low-emission targets would reduce ice loss by 2100 compared with high-emission scenarios.
claims.source_title: Today's emissions choices could limit Antarctic ice loss and sea-level rise for coastal communities
claims.supporting_quote: The team found at least an 89% probability that the most ambitious low-emission goal consistent with the objectives of the Paris Agreement would result in less Antarctic ice loss by the end of the century than a scenario with very high emissions.

claims.claim: Experiments with hydrogels and water droplets showed no measurable acceleration of evaporation attributable to visible light exposure alone.
claims.episode_span: Direct measurements showed no measurable acceleration attributable to light exposure alone.
claims.source_title: Visible light does not speed up water evaporation, rigorous experiments suggest
claims.supporting_quote: In recent experiments involving hydrogels and water droplets, researchers have proposed that exposure to visible light could make water evaporate faster without heating it. However, direct evidence that light acts on water itself has proven elusive.
